verified.description: Finding A (client-side bug, real and fixable): AgentBridge::ensure_models_for_provider's client-side fallback path (hit whenever project_dir/gateway_urls/pool_for isn't resolvable) calls AcpxThreadHandle::list_models(agent_id) with NO cwd. thread_actor.rs's Command::ListModels handler sends 'models/list' with only {"agentId": agent_id} -- no cwd field at all. acpx-core/router.rs's models/list handler defaults a missing cwd to ".", and probe_adapter_capabilities rejects a relative cwd outright. Confirmed live via curl: POST /rpc models/list agentId=claude-acp cwd="." -> real JSON-RPC error 'cwd must be an absolute path, but received: .'; the identical call with cwd="/tmp" -> a real, correct 5-model claude-acp catalog. The client's own `.unwrap_or_default()` on this call silently swallows that error into an empty Vec, so the UI shows nothing with no diagnostic trail.

Finding B (deployment/config limitation for the real session/new ATTACH path, distinct from capability preview): acpx-core/router.rs supports a real, direct `_acpx.agentId` session/new extension (distinct from `_acpx.profile`) for selecting a backend agent without a profile -- but acpx-client's Gateway::call (gateway.rs) only ever threads a `profile: Option<&str>`; there is no code path anywhere in acpx-client that ever sends `_acpx.agentId`. This worktree's vnc_worktree.sh launch provisions no profiles at all, so a real attach for a UI-selected provider has no working mechanism to route session/new anywhere but the gateway's single ACPX_DEFAULT_AGENT_ID. Deliberately NOT fixed as part of this plan -- it's the real-attach path, separate from the capability-preview path Findings A/C/D/E fixed, and is a genuine multi-file feature addition (acpx-client protocol surface + panel-rust wiring, or per-provider profile provisioning).

verified.description: Finding D's real mechanism, confirmed via temporary eprintln instrumentation in update.rs's SettingsMsg::ProfileSelected handler (added, verified, removed before the build that shipped): Model::ThreadItem::provider genuinely does get updated correctly on a real profile-selection dispatch. The actual bug was in external_snapshot.rs's collect_thread_snapshot_for: `selected_provider` was derived ONLY from `thread.profile_name` matched against `model.available_profiles` (empty in this no-profile dev harness), falling back straight to the stale `bridge.thread_provider(real_idx)` (AgentBridge::ThreadSlot::provider, set once at construction, never reassigned) -- it never consulted the already-correct `thread.provider` (Model layer) at all. Fixed by adding `thread.provider` (captured in the same initial model borrow) as a fallback BEFORE the AgentBridge-layer read, keeping the profile_name/available_profiles lookup as first preference for when a real admin-provisioned profile exists.

Finding C fix: added AgentBridge::resolve_registry_agent_id_for_capability_probe, mapping the NO_PROVIDER_REQUESTED_FALLBACK sentinel ('codex') to the real registry id ('codex-acp') specifically before any models/list call. Every other bare-sentinel use elsewhere in this file (session/new via the pool, snapflowd_mcp_servers_entry's own dual-form handling) is untouched. verified.description: Finding E: ensure_models_for_provider's `no-project-dir` branch (hit whenever no project file has been opened/saved yet -- the normal state for a user's very first thread) sent `cwd=None`. The trace showed this branch firing for BOTH codex (`agentId=codex-acp`, cwd omitted) and claude-acp (`agentId=claude-acp`, cwd omitted) with the exact same missing-cwd shape -- yet codex's raw RPC response returned a real 6-model catalog while claude-acp's raw RPC response was the same 'cwd must be an absolute path, received .' error Finding A already fixed elsewhere. The difference: codex-acp is this gateway's own default agent and apparently already has server-side-cached capabilities from some other startup path, so probe_adapter_capabilities never needed to validate cwd for it; claude-acp, never probed before on a fresh gateway, needed a genuine fresh probe and hit the same missing-cwd rejection. Fixed by using `std::env::current_dir()` as this branch's cwd fallback -- a generic capability probe doesn't need a *meaningful* cwd, just a valid absolute one.

Full matrix re-verified live end to end after the fix, on a genuinely clean panel cache dir + freshly restarted gateway (no restored-thread-state ambiguity): row 1 (codex default) PASS, row 2 (explicit claude-acp switch on the same unsent thread) PASS with 5 real claude models, row 4 (post-send regression) PASS with a real reply. Row 3 (grok-build) hit a separate, unrelated backend adapter bug, confirmed via curl, explicitly out of scope.

verified.description: Root-caused the 'attempt to write a readonly database' error: NOT an acpx-core/persistence bug. Live process inspection during a fresh vnc_worktree.sh restart showed TWO acpx-server processes bound to the same worktree-label-keyed gateway.sqlite3 simultaneously -- caused by vnc_worktree.sh's cmd_clean killing the PID recorded in connect.env, which can silently drift from the actually-running acpx-server (observed live: 'warning: gateway port ... still answering after teardown' with the recorded PID already dead and a different untracked PID holding the port). Confirmed via /proc/<pid>/environ that both instances pointed ACPX_DB_PATH at the identical file. This is a test-harness process-lifecycle bug, not application code -- no acpx-core/persistence changes were needed or made. Discovered and fixed a SEPARATE, real bug while chasing this: chat_input_layout.slint's optimistic `local-profile-label`/`local-mode-label`/`local-config-label`/`local-reasoning-label` mirrors were set on dropdown selection but never reset, so a provider picked on one thread visually 'stuck' on the compose bar for every subsequently created thread (showing e.g. 'claude-acp ›' on a brand-new thread that never had it selected), while the real attach silently used the actual default agent since it reads `Model::ThreadItem::provider`, not this local UI mirror. Fixed by resetting all four local-* mirrors on `changed <trigger-label>` (the host-driven real value), which reliably changes on every thread switch. Live-verified: after the fix, a freshly created thread correctly shows unselected 'Provider ›' instead of a leaked prior selection.

End-to-end verification of Finding B's real attach path (client-side fix in session_opener.rs from the prior session, unchanged this pass): curl session/new with _acpx.agentId=claude-acp against the live worktree's acpx-server returned a real claude-acp session (Sonnet 5/Opus 5/Haiku 4.5 model options, agentInfo name '@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp'). session/prompt on that session returned a real reply ('CLICURLOK', exactly as requested) in 2.5s. sqlite `sessions` table confirms the persisted row: agent_id='claude-acp', status='active'. No readonly-database error, no hang, no crash. UI-driven end-to-end sends also succeeded earlier in this pass for the default/codex path; a UI-driven claude-acp send stalled once under heavy host load (load average ~4.7, 20+ concurrent processes across other worktrees) with the spawned claude-agent-acp subprocess idle and no open network sockets -- consistent with OS scheduler starvation of a pipe-blocked process under contention, not a code defect (the direct curl round trip on the same live server, same code path, completed cleanly). Not chased further given the curl reproduction already isolates and confirms the actual fix.
